A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DocLayLLM and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables and appendices. Their shared content can be matched reliably despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original document-understanding benchmark results, component ablations and qualitative examples, including an OCRBench comparison in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional modality comparisons, input-length measurements and OCR-source testing.

M1.justification: The architecture, embedding/projector operations, three CoT pre-training procedures and CoT annealing strategy remain substantively unchanged. Newly specified image resolution, initialization and trainable modules document implementation rather than establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The training corpora and main VQA, KIE and table-understanding benchmarks remain unchanged. v3 Appendix E adds a DocVQA test scenario using commercial rather than official OCR output. The removed OCRBench subset uses retained FUNSD, SROIE and POIE data, so its removal does not eliminate those task domains.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds LMDX, reporting 66.95 on CORD. The separate comparison against InternVL2-8B and GPT-4o in v1 Appendix A.3/Table 8 disappears. The other main benchmark comparator sets remain substantially intact; the layout-to-coor suffix change is a renaming.

E3.justification: v3 adds modality controls, a Llama3-tokenizer input-length evaluation and an official-versus-commercial OCR testing protocol. It removes the 200-sample OCRBench evaluation. Main training budgets and hyperparameters remain unchanged; explicitly documenting full-scale SFT for ablations does not establish a budget change.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analysis beyond the retained CoT, initialization and patch ablations. Table 5b compares text-only, textual coordinates and embedded coordinates; Appendix D measures input length; Appendix E tests OCR-source sensitivity and illustrates error correction. Figure A also adds qualitative comparisons with and without each CoT component.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Benchmark averages and average input lengths do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported values change materially: Llama2-7B-Chat DocVQA changes from 64.99 in v1 Table 2 to 20.50 in v3 Table 1; downstream-trained DocLayLLM VisualMRC changes from 388.85 to 327.91. Ablation VisualMRC scores also change. v3 adds modality, input-length and OCR results, including 86.52 versus 87.52 DocVQA ANLS, while removing OCRBench results and the seven-benchmark zero-shot row from v1 Table 5. These revisions do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the geometric reasoning underlying the CoT procedures retain their mathematical substance. Indexing changes and worked illustrations add explanation, without introducing new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 foregrounds CoT Pre-training as a method for generating large-scale CoT data from non-QA annotations, whereas v1 primarily presents its contribution as improving training efficiency and comprehension. The central architectural, efficiency and comparative-performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific interpretations that CoT annealing encourages direct yes/no answers, layout embeddings improve efficiency through shorter inputs, and alternative OCR results and error correction support practical robustness. These extend v1's broader explanations of CoT, layout integration and generalization.

D1.justification: v3 provides a code/model availability link, identifies TextIn OCR, and specifies 224×224 images, 196 patch tokens, random projector initialization and trainable embedding/projector modules. The detailed hyperparameter table, hardware and training-time disclosures already existed in v1. Resource availability is stated in the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands cited background on document encoders and recent MLLMs, including DocFormerv2, LayoutLMv2, LLaVA-OneVision and Idefics3. It adds LMDX and positions CoT data generation alongside DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ. The earlier standalone positioning against general MLLMs in Appendix A.3 is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion receive extensive editing and reframing. Qualitative results gain a main-text subsection, and the appendix is reorganized into sections A–E, including relocation of the pre-training task list. The title, affiliations and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds a CoT illustration, processed-pre-training-data columns, a two-part ablation table, input-length and OCR tables, and new qualitative panels. Existing KIE examples move into the main text, other examples are reorganized into Figure A, and the OCRBench table disappears. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The expanded modality controls and input-length/OCR analyses better support the architecture's efficiency and practical behavior. Added implementation details and stated code/model access improve reproducibility. These gains are moderated by removal of the OCRBench comparison and some zero-shot results, plus unexplained numerical revisions. Overall, v3 provides clearer and stronger support for the same core method, yielding a limited net improvement.
